q: Do the QWC/FC grouping benefits (2-4x for QWC, ~50x for FC on LiH) survive when evaluated at realistic VQE trial states (UCCSD or hardware-efficient ansaetze near their variational minima) instead of the exact ground state?
basis: Our LiH result (QWC 3.03x, FC 53.8x) was computed at the exact ground state via dense diagonalization. Real VQE runs measure w.r.t. a parametrized trial state; per-fragment variances can differ substantially near approximate minima, and the review does not report ansatz-conditioned variance surfaces for the specific molecules we tested.
next_steps: Rebuild the H_alpha fragments for LiH, run a short VQE loop with a UCCSD ansatz (e.g. Qiskit Nature VQE + statevector), record per-fragment variances at each iterate, and recompute M_opt at the converged theta*. Compare M_opt(theta*) to M_opt(ground state) and report the ratio for QWC and FC. Repeat for a hardware-efficient ansatz to check ansatz sensitivity.

q: How does the sample-cost reduction from Pauli grouping compare against modern classical-shadow variants (locally-biased / derandomized shadows) on the same LiH-scale Hamiltonian?
basis: The paper reviews both grouping and shadow-based estimators but does not provide a like-for-like head-to-head on a fixed molecule. Our replication only reproduced the grouping side (baseline: naive single-Pauli-per-shot). Whether FC grouping still wins against a well-tuned locally-biased shadow protocol on LiH is not settled by our data.
next_steps: Implement locally-biased classical shadows (Hadamard-Huang-Preskill 2020 + Hadfield derandomization 2022) for the LiH Hamiltonian; hold the total shot budget fixed; measure realized MSE of the energy estimator over 200 repeats at 1.5k / 15k / 150k shots; compare directly to the FC-grouping-with-optimal-allocation numbers we already have in grouping_summary_v3.json.

q: Does the FC>QWC ordering hold for strongly-correlated systems (stretched N2, Cr2, or a small transition-metal complex) where the Hamiltonian has qualitatively different Pauli-term statistics?
basis: Our tests were H2 (weakly correlated) and LiH at equilibrium (mildly correlated). Strongly-correlated ground states have heavier-tailed off-diagonal coefficient distributions; the greedy coloring heuristic could behave very differently. The review discusses FC>QWC generically but does not stress-test it against strong correlation.
next_steps: Build stretched-N2 (R=2.5 A, STO-3G or cc-pVDZ frozen-core) and Cr2 (STO-3G, active space CAS(12,12)) Hamiltonians via PySCF, apply the existing measurement_grouping_v3.py pipeline unchanged, and report M_opt ungrouped / QWC / FC plus reduction factors. Flag any case where FC ceases to dominate QWC.

q: How robust is the grouping-based sample-cost reduction to realistic device noise (readout error, coherent gate error on the joint diagonalization circuits required by FC groups)?
basis: FC groups require a joint Clifford diagonalization circuit before measurement, which adds gate depth. On noisy hardware the added error could offset the sample-cost win. Our replication was noise-free statevector simulation; the review acknowledges but does not quantify this trade-off for the FC>QWC comparison.
next_steps: For H2 (small enough to be tractable), run the QWC and FC measurement protocols through Qiskit's FakeManila / FakeGuadalupe noise model plus a parametrized readout-error channel (0.1% to 5%). Measure realized MSE per total shot vs noise level; find the crossover noise strength at which QWC beats FC despite having a worse noiseless bound.

q: Can an ML-driven shot-budget allocator (trained on pilot samples of per-fragment variance) beat the sqrt(Var)-optimal allocation the paper prescribes, when per-fragment variances are only approximately known?
basis: The paper's M_opt = (sum sqrt(Var_alpha))^2 assumes exact knowledge of Var(H_alpha). In practice these are estimated from a small pilot batch and are themselves noisy; naive plug-in of noisy sqrt(Var_hat_alpha) can waste shots. This mismatch is acknowledged in the classical-shadow literature but not deeply treated in the review's grouping sections.
next_steps: Simulate the two-stage protocol: (a) pilot batch of K shots per fragment for K in {10, 50, 200}; (b) allocate remaining budget by plug-in sqrt(Var_hat). Compare realized MSE to (i) the ideal known-variance sqrt(Var) allocation and (ii) a small bandit-style allocator (Thompson sampling over per-fragment variance posteriors). Report the pilot-K at which the bandit stops helping. Do this on LiH FC groups (35 arms) using the existing statevector infrastructure.
